statement: The condition number of a function measures how sensitive the function output is to small changes or errors in the input argument, formally defined as the asymptotic worst-case ratio of the relative change in output to the relative change in input: for a function $f$ at a point $x$, $\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0^+} \sup_{\|\delta x\| \le \varepsilon} \left[ \frac{\|f(x+\delta x) - f(x)\|}{\|f(x)\|} \Big/ \frac{\|\delta x\|}{\|x\|} \right]$; for a linear system $Ax = b$ with a nonsingular matrix $A$, it is the maximum ratio of the relative error in $x$ to the relative error in $b$, given by $\kappa(A) = \|A^{-1}\| \|A\|$.

symbols.meaning: function mapping data from a domain to a codomain (Banach spaces)
small change or perturbation in the input argument x
square or rectangular matrix defining the linear problem Ax = b
symbols.dimensions: n x n (or m x n)

symbols.meaning: right-hand side data vector in linear system Ax = b
error or perturbation vector in data vector b
matrix inverse of nonsingular matrix A
norm on vector space or induced operator norm on matrices
Jacobian matrix of partial derivatives of f evaluated at x
maximal and minimal singular values of matrix A

properties.property: Under the matrix norm induced by the Euclidean $L_2$ norm, $\kappa(A) = \frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)}{\sigma_{\min}(A)}$.
properties.why: The induced $L_2$ norm of $A$ is its largest singular value and $\|A^{-1}\|_2 = 1/\sigma_{\min}(A)$

properties.property: If $A$ is a normal matrix, under the $L_2$ norm $\kappa(A) = \frac{\max\{|\lambda(A)|\}}{\min\{|\lambda(A)|\}}$.
properties.why: Singular values of a normal matrix are the moduli of its eigenvalues
All singular values of a unitary matrix equal 1

properties.property: If $f$ is differentiable, the relative condition number at $x$ is $\frac{\|J(x)\|}{\|f(x)\| / \|x\|}$.
properties.why: The infinitesimal limit of the relative perturbation ratio converges to the induced norm of the Jacobian $J(x)$ scaled by $\|x\|/\|f(x)\|$

properties.property: For a differentiable single-variable function $f$, the relative condition number at $x$ is $|x f'(x) / f(x)| = |(\log f)' / (\log x)'|$.
properties.why: Taking the infinitesimal limit of relative changes yields the ratio of logarithmic derivatives

properties.property: If $\|\cdot\|$ is induced by the $L^\infty$ norm and $A$ is lower triangular and nonsingular, $\kappa(A) \ge \frac{\max_i (|a_{ii}|)}{\min_i (|a_{ii}|)}$.
properties.why: The eigenvalues of a triangular matrix are its diagonal entries $a_{ii}$

properties.property: For rectangular or non-invertible matrices, the condition number can be defined as $\kappa(A) = \|A\| \|A^\dagger\|$.
properties.why: Replaces the matrix inverse with the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse $A^\dagger$

properties.property: If $\kappa(A) = 10^k$, up to $k$ digits of accuracy may be lost on top of arithmetic precision loss.
properties.why: The condition number bounds the worst-case magnification of relative error from input to output

assumptions.assumption: The matrix $A$ is nonsingular and invertible for the standard formulation $\kappa(A) = \|A^{-1}\| \|A\|$.
assumptions.breaks_when: The matrix $A$ is singular or rectangular, requiring the pseudoinverse formulation $A^\dagger$ or resulting in $\kappa(A) = \infty$.

assumptions.assumption: The input data $x$ and function output $f(x)$ (or linear system vectors $b$ and $x$) are non-zero.
assumptions.breaks_when: The input $x = 0$ or output $f(x) = 0$, which causes division by zero in relative change ratios.
A non-consistent norm is used, invalidating the lower bound $\kappa(A) \ge \|A^{-1}A\| = 1$.

assumptions.assumption: The function $f$ is differentiable at point $x$ for the derivative/Jacobian representations.
assumptions.breaks_when: $f$ is not differentiable at $x$, preventing the reduction of the supremum limit to the Jacobian operator norm.

failure_modes.signature: Computed solution $x$ exhibits large errors despite small errors in input data $b$, losing up to $k$ digits of precision when $\kappa(A) = 10^k$.
failure_modes.cause: Condition number $\kappa(A)$ is very large, meaning $A$ is nearly singular and strongly magnifies input inaccuracies.

failure_modes.signature: $\kappa(A) = \infty$, and numerical algorithms fail to reliably determine a solution.
failure_modes.cause: The matrix $A$ is non-invertible/singular, meaning the system does not possess a unique, well-defined solution for each choice of data.

failure_modes.signature: Relative condition number of $f$ diverges to infinity at $x$.
failure_modes.cause: $f(x) = 0$, causing infinitesimal changes in input to produce an infinite relative change in output due to division by zero.
